heading: How we deliver and <hl>keep delivering</hl>
intro: A six-step loop, not a one-way project. We work one priority use case at a time, taking each from discovery to governed, Cortex-powered data in production on Snowflake, then start the next. The governed, AI-ready foundation grows with the business as we keep delivering.

steps.title: Discover
steps.desc: Assess the current estate, data sources, and business goals; define success metrics.

steps.title: Design
steps.desc: Architect the target Snowflake platform, governance model, and semantic layer.

steps.title: Migrate & Ingest
steps.desc: Move and connect data with automated translation, validation, and Openflow pipelines.

steps.title: Build
steps.desc: Engineer data products, analytics, and Cortex AI / agentic workloads on governed data.

steps.title: Govern & Validate
steps.desc: Apply Horizon Catalog lineage, access controls, and PII classification, with shared business context in Semantic Views so every team and AI agent reads one set of definitions; test for trust.

steps.title: Run & Optimize
steps.desc: Operate, monitor, and tune consumption and performance, with enablement for the in-house team.

why.title: A partner who knows the whole journey

items.title: The whole modern data stack, not one tool
items.body: Ingestion (Openflow, Snowpipe Streaming), transformation (dbt, Snowpark, Dynamic Tables), governance (Horizon Catalog, and Horizon Context once it is generally available), analytics (Snowsight, Streamlit), and AI agents (Cortex, Snowflake CoWork), all centered on one governed Snowflake core.

items.title: Governed and open by design
items.body: Built on Apache Iceberg and Open Catalog (Polaris) so data stays interoperable across engines and clouds.

items.title: Get it right the first time
items.body: Proven migration frameworks and certified architects reduce risk and rework when moving off Teradata, Oracle, Hadoop, or SQL Server.

items.title: Beyond dashboards to data agents
items.body: We ground Snowflake CoWork (the personal AI agent) and Cortex Agents in governed Semantic Views, so business users get cited, trustworthy answers from the same definitions every team uses.
